demotions.reason: Gate 8 materially weakened/failed for the broad wedge: enterprise OMS/payment integrations already implement fulfillment-aware authorization reversal, including automatic reversal strategies for unfulfilled, expired, cancelled and excess authorizations.

rejections.fatal_flaw: IBM Sterling OMS has configurable authorization-reversal strategies that automatically create reversal requests and call PSP cancel APIs; Adyen's Salesforce OMS integration exposes authorization reversal specifically when an order can no longer be fulfilled. The remaining fee-deadline overlay is too narrow to sustain the prior 49/60 score without incidence evidence.

current_leader_detail.why_survived: Still read-only, deterministic fee delta, cross-cloud recurring paid support tiers, and no exact continuous cross-cloud telemetry-aware support-tier optimizer established in prior research.

runner_ups.note: demoted from 47 because Stripe already prevents some retry penalties and fee-intelligence vendors cover much of surrounding space

strongest_evidence: Visa states misuse-of-authorization fees apply when approved authorizations cannot be matched to clearing or reversal.
Chase states unused Mastercard authorizations must be reversed within 24h card-present or 72h card-not-present.
IBM Sterling OMS already implements configurable automatic authorization reversal for expired/unfulfilled orders and excess authorizations.
Adyen Salesforce OMS authorization reversal handles orders that can no longer be fulfilled.
Recivr prices authorization/capture/reversal fee events and surfaces authorization-related pure cost.
new_search_rules: Do not confuse an available PSP reversal API with whitespace: enterprise OMS layers may already connect fulfillment state to automatic reversal.
When the narrow wedge is a rules/deadline overlay on an action already automated by OMS, require strong incidence evidence before treating the overlay as defensible.
